## Vocabulary

- **self**: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint (15/2)

## Definitions

- [statement] The documented success payload is an array containing orgId, resourceId, resourceName, resourceType, and resourcePoliciesCausingNonCompliance; nested entries identify resourcePolicyId, resourcePolicyName, and policiesCausingNonCompliance[].policyId. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://www.withone.ai/knowledge/mongo-db-atlas-administration/conn_mod_def%3A%3AGJ4_1NI5agE%3A%3AFIuB2LCpSeirBrBvHRVLQQ

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB recommends proactively monitoring this endpoint because resource policies do not enforce all intermediate or transitional states; downstream failures can leave a temporary non-compliant state. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A practical monitoring pattern is to poll this endpoint, feed results into configuration-drift alerting, and track remediation or documented exceptions; this is operational guidance rather than a documented push-notification feature. (medium confidence) — https://howtoharden.com/guides/mongodb-atlas/ · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/nonCompliantResources returns non-compliant resources for an organization; MongoDB’s Go SDK index exposes the same route as GetNonCompliantResources. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://github.com/mongodb/atlas-sdk-go/blob/main/docs/doc_last_reference.md, https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/
- [statement] The API reference lists Organization Member as the role requirement. orgId is required and is a 24-hexadecimal string. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] The documented resourceType values are PROJECT, CLUSTER, DEPRECATED_PROJECT and DEPRECATED_CLUSTER; do not assume a separate NETWORK enum from informal descriptions of network violations. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] The endpoint documents envelope and pretty boolean query options, both defaulting to false. Its default response example is a JSON array. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] Applying a resource policy does not automatically remediate existing resources. Foojay’s August 13, 2025 walkthrough reports that an existing 0.0.0.0/0 entry remained and was flagged after a wildcard-blocking policy was applied. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/
- [statement] Existing autoscaling limits can permit automatic scaling beyond a newly applied policy even though manual scaling beyond policy limits is blocked. MongoDB recommends identifying these resources with nonCompliantResources and updating them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] Integrate nonCompliantResources polling with configuration-drift monitoring and route returned resources to remediation; MongoDB recommends proactive monitoring, and How to Harden explicitly recommends wiring the query into drift alerting. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://howtoharden.com/guides/mongodb-atlas/
- [statement] The Resource Policies endpoint set shares an ORGANIZATION-scoped token bucket: capacity 500 and refill 250 tokens per 60 seconds. nonCompliantResources shares that bucket with resource-policy CRUD and validation endpoints. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/api-rate-limit.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] The API reference includes the CLI command atlas api resourcePolicies getNonCompliantResources --help and examples for bearer-token and HTTP Digest authentication. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] The API reference lists Organization Member as its role requirement and documents service-account bearer authentication and API-key Digest authentication examples. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-getorgnoncompliantresources · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] MongoDB recommends proactive monitoring: downstream failures can leave intermediate states non-compliant, and clusters with pre-existing autoscaling limits beyond a new policy can continue scaling automatically beyond those boundaries even though manual scaling is constrained. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint
- [statement] After an Atlas Resource Policy is applied, Atlas only allows changes to an existing non-compliant cluster that bring it into compliance; if the policy blocks AWS, MongoDB's example says the cluster can only be switched to Azure or Google Cloud. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Atlas nonCompliantResources endpoint · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
